subject: Clarify SPV vs Processor obligations for US-state privacy addendum
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@heliotech.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@heliotech.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify role: SPV vs Processor for US-state addendum

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking this — we are reviewing Redwood's standard DPA and the US-state addendum Helio is preparing. Two quick asks from our legal/privacy team:

1) For CCPA/CPRA and related state privacy laws, does Redwood position itself as a Service Provider/Operator (i.e., limited use) or as a Processor (broader processing authority) in your US-state addendum?
2) We need to confirm how telemetry (inference logs, error traces, and aggregated usage metrics) is treated. Is telemetry considered "service-provided telemetry" (limited use for service improvement) or does it count as a separate processing purpose that would require Helio to run a sale/transfer analysis under CCPA?

Attached is a coarse dataflow we pulled together — it shows inference requests, KV cache, and third-party CDNs. We also included a redline of your DPA with Helio's suggested language (HelioTech_DPA_Redlines.docx). Can you review and advise the right contract position and any evidence we should provide (onshore fallback, encryption-in-transit-at-rest proof) to keep Helio in the Service Provider lane?

Appreciate a short call if easier.

Best,
Maya Rao
Senior Counsel — Privacy
HelioTech Systems
[Attachment: HT_DataFlow_Diagram.pdf]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@heliotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify role: SPV vs Processor for US-state addendum

Maya —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the diagram + redlines. Short answer up front: Redwood's standard position for hosted/Dedicated customers is to act as a Service Provider / "Service Provider" as defined in the CCPA/CPRA addendum (limited-use), provided the customer pins processing purposes to inference, caching, and operational troubleshooting. We push back on wording that would permit broad ancillary uses (e.g., marketing).

Telemetry: inference-level telemetry (latency, error codes, aggregate token counts) is treated as operational telemetry for service improvement and fraud/detection. We do not use customer-provided prompts for model training unless explicitly contracted. That telemetry treatment is typically included in a specific clause in the US-state addendum (we call it "Operational Telemetry and Limited Use").

To help HelioTech keep this in the SP lane, we usually provide:
- a short, annotated dataflow showing where telemetry is transient and how KV/prefix caches are isolated per-tenant;
- logging retention windows and deletion proof points (we can share retention policies and a sample log retention report);
- confirmation of onshore fallback options for telemetry and a description of encryption-at-rest/in-transit for telemetry stores;
- a commitment to 30-day subprocessor notice and 14-day emergency on-board for critical subprocessors (we can negotiate exact windows).

I'm looping in Marissa (privacy lead) and Aditya (infra) to pick up the redlines and prepare the evidence pack. If HelioTech wants a quick call we can do 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the redlines.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Director — Redwood Inference
[Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleLink]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@heliotech.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify role: SPV vs Processor for US-state addendum

Maya / team —

Reviewing Helio's redlines now. A few notes we plan to propose instead of Helio's current edits:

- Narrow "Purpose" language: we'll agree to inference, infrastructure ops, and security/stability. We'll explicitly exclude marketing and model training beyond aggregated quality metrics unless separately contracted.

- Telemetry definition: propose defining three buckets (a) transient request metadata (latency/error/sample id), (b) aggregated usage metrics (non-identifiable aggregates), (c) customer-provided content (prompts). Buckets (a)/(b) remain Service Provider-limited; (c) is not used for model training.

- Subprocessor clause: Redwood provides a rolling subprocessor list via portal and 30 days' notice for non-critical additions; for emergency critical additions (zero-day infra fixes) we will notify within 48 hours and provide mitigation documentation.

- Evidence pack: Aditya and Priya will produce a short pack (dataflow PDF with callouts, retention policy excerpt, and a sample log purge report). We can redact any infra-specific hostnames.

If Helio wants stronger contractual language (e.g., audit rights), we'll need to take that to sales/legal as it changes commercial terms. For now we can stay in the SP lane with the proposed edits; I'll attach a concise redline to your doc and flag any commercial-impacting asks.

Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Trust — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SPV_annotated_redline.docx]

From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@heliotech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@heliotech.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify role: SPV vs Processor for US-state addendum

Marissa / Sean —

Thanks, that level of detail is perfect. Helio's privacy counsel reviewed your proposed buckets and the 30/48 hour subprocessors approach looks workable. Two immediate asks before we finalize redlines:

1) Please send the annotated dataflow PDF (redact hosts as needed) and the sample log purge report — our compliance team will want to keep those in Helio's internal evidence repository.
2) Can Redwood confirm the retention window for transient request metadata (bucket a) in writing? Helio prefers 45 days, but we can consider shorter windows if there's a documented operational reason.

If you can deliver the evidence pack and a one-paragraph retention commitment, we should be able to finalize the addendum without commercial changes. Hoping to close this week.

Best,
Maya Rao
Senior Counsel — Privacy
HelioTech Systems
[Received: HT_DataFlow_Diagram.pdf, HelioTech_DPA_Redlines.docx]
